answer: New identities must forge a proof-of-work artifact before they can transact: each applicant runs a verifiable delay function whose output is woven into a short signed sonnet and pinned to the admission ledge, a public board peers inspect before activation. One forge costs about ten minutes of compute and is tied to the applicant's hardware key, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand forges plus a thousand distinct keys, and any two artifacts sharing a forge fingerprint are rejected outright, collapsing the attacker's army to only the identities they actually paid to build.
